note: Most of the list is the brass bands themselves: Pagador and the Poopó bands of Oruro, and the Puno bands Super Impacto and the Peruvian police band. The rest are folk groups (Inti-Illimani, Illapu, Kjarkas, Zulma Yugar, Jaime Torres) playing pieces their records name as morenadas or diabladas.

size.basis: No source counts recordings. English Wikipedia says the Oruro Carnival alone has about 10,000 musicians in 150 bands. Bands put out long albums made up only of morenadas or diabladas (Pagador's Morenadas Tradicionales de Bolivia has 31 tracks; a Puno band's Diablada Azoguini anthology has 36). The iTunes catalogue shows many more band albums and yearly singles from Oruro, Puno and northern Chile (Arica, Tocopilla, Antofagasta), and Andean folk groups have recorded hundreds of morenada and diablada arrangements since the 1960s. An insider's essential list is about 40 pieces.
